newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-GERMANY'S FIRST WORLD CUP MATCH THREATENED BY VIOLENCE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GERMANY'S FIRST WORLD CUP MATCH THREATENED BY VIOLENCE.

text.p: Germany's opening World Cup qualifier against Armenia in Yerevan on October 9 could be postponed or moved to another venue following civil unrest there.
The German soccer federation (DFB) said on Thursday it was concerned about violence in Armenia and would seek advice from the Foreign Ministry on whether the match can go ahead.
Thousands of opposition demonstrators clashed with police on Wednesday in the capital following elections there last Sunday.

"We are following the developments carefully, calmly and without wanting to cause any panic," said DFB spokesman Michael Novak on Thursday. "We are in contact with FIFA and on the political level as well."
He said that the DFB did not want to overdramatise the situation and would seek guidance from Germany's embassy in the former Soviet republic.
Trouble broke out on Wednesday after Armenian President Levon Ter-Petrosyan was re-elected.
Opposition supporters took to the streets of Yerevan in protest at alleged vote-rigging and were tear-gassed by police. Some reports said 59 demonstrators had been hurt and one killed.
Ter-Petrosyan, a 50-year-old academic, has ruled Armenia for five years, since it became independent on the collapse of the Soviet Union.
